headline: A Verge writer who is testing AI models on a Mac Studio instead of in the cloud says a free local assistant handled private tasks and sorted a 400-game Steam library, but setup was overwhelming and a daily briefing kept breaking.
score_reason: Kept at 4: new on 11 Oct 2026 and read in full, but it is one writer's early diary on a very high-end machine, not a test with measured results.
importance_line: People who do not want to send private data to cloud AI services may see that a free local assistant can already do small chores on a very high-end home computer, but this is one writer's early diary, the machine has 256GB of memory, and the writer says local AI is no magic assistant and the briefing broke several times.
summary: The Verge publishes a first-person diary in which its writer, testing an M5 Ultra Mac Studio with 256GB of memory, installs the free open-source Hermes Agent app and the Qwen 3.8 Flash Next model (125 billion parameters) and uses them on the computer itself to build a daily briefing, sort a Steam library of more than 400 games and analyse financial records and an embargoed laptop spec list, tasks the writer would not give to a cloud service. The writer calls the experience exciting, overwhelming and frustrating: the briefing broke several times, a script to automate benchmark tests is unfinished, and even powerful local models are no magical assistant.
notes: Read The Verge in full. First-person diary; the writer is not named in the fetched text. Not a reply story.
